subsystems.name: Quantum sensing element
subsystems.role: the physical system whose quantum state shifts in response to whatever is being measured — a field, acceleration, rotation or time.
parts: cold-atom cloud or atomic vapour cell

subsystems.name: Control and interrogation
subsystems.role: prepares the quantum state and reads out its shift.

subsystems.name: Isolation environment
subsystems.role: protects fragile quantum coherence from stray fields, vibration and heat.

subsystems.name: Readout chain
subsystems.role: converts the tiny quantum signal into an electrical one.

subsystems.name: Signal processing and timing
subsystems.role: turns phase shifts, precession frequencies or photon counts into a usable measurement.

subsystems.name: Field-deployable package
subsystems.role: makes the instrument survive outside a laboratory.
parts: mounting on vehicle, aircraft, borehole or body

buildSteps.title: Choose the platform
buildSteps.detail: Decide what physics to exploit: atomic precession for fields and rotation, atom interference for gravity and acceleration, superconducting loops for faint magnetic fields, or photons for imaging.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate the sensing element
buildSteps.detail: Grow diamond and implant nitrogen atoms to form vacancy centres; or machine a vacuum cell and load it with an alkali metal; or pattern Josephson junctions for a SQUID.

buildSteps.title: Build the control optics and electronics
buildSteps.detail: Assemble stabilised lasers, modulators, microwave chains and a frequency comb, then align them to cool, trap and interrogate the atoms.

buildSteps.title: Isolate the system
buildSteps.detail: Enclose the sensor in magnetic shielding and vacuum, and add cooling and vibration isolation so external noise does not swamp the signal.

buildSteps.title: Wire up the readout
buildSteps.detail: Fit photodetectors or amplifier chains that record the state with enough sensitivity to resolve a small shift.

buildSteps.title: Calibrate and process
buildSteps.detail: Measure against a known reference, then run algorithms that convert the raw signal into a field value, an acceleration or a time.

buildSteps.title: Ruggedise and shrink
buildSteps.detail: Replace laboratory hardware with chip-scale lasers, integrated photonics and low-power electronics so the device can leave the bench.

buildSteps.title: Validate in the field
buildSteps.detail: Deploy for geophysical surveys, medical scanning or navigation trials, and characterise drift, temperature sensitivity and reliability.

prerequisites.why: cold, slow atoms give long measurement times and hence extreme sensitivity.

prerequisites.tech: Narrow-linewidth lasers and optical frequency combs
prerequisites.why: they interrogate quantum states precisely and count optical frequencies.
ambient fields and collisions destroy the coherence the measurement depends on.
superconducting sensors need very low temperatures and specialist junction fabrication.
nitrogen-vacancy centres work in the lab, but placing them reproducibly at scale is still maturing.

prerequisites.tech: Compact, low-power control electronics and integrated photonics
prerequisites.why: bench-scale lasers and optics must shrink before sensors become field instruments.

pathway.milestone: atomic clocks in satellite navigation and telecom networks, cryogenic SQUID magnetometers, and cold-atom gravimeters used in geophysical and engineering surveys
pathway.unlocks: timekeeping, brain and heart magnetic imaging, and detection of voids, tunnels and ore bodies.

pathway.milestone: portable, cryogen-free magnetometers and field gravimeters, including optically pumped sensors
pathway.unlocks: cheaper medical scanning without liquid helium and routine underground and mineral mapping.

pathway.milestone: chip-scale cold-atom inertial sensors for navigation without satellite signals
pathway.unlocks: positioning for ships, aircraft and vehicles where GNSS is jammed or unavailable.

pathway.milestone: entanglement-enhanced and networked sensing below the classical noise limit
pathway.unlocks: distributed arrays for security, environmental monitoring and tests of fundamental physics.
